svg.text: Lossless RoCE on SONiC: how the CONFIG_DB QoS/buffer tables reference each other
What nv set qos roce does in one line, SONiC expresses as ~12 tables. Arrows = key references (pipe-separated compound keys)

g.title: BUFFER_POOL ingress_lossless_pool type ingress · mode dynamic · size
SCHEDULER scheduler.0 STRICT · scheduler.1 DWRR weight 50
PORT Ethernet0 lanes 0-3 · 400000 · mtu 9100 · fec rs
Packet pipeline (ingress → egress) and where PFC/ECN act

svg.text: Packet pipeline (ingress → egress) and where PFC/ECN act
Headroom intuition (why xoff/xon are platform-computed): the switch must absorb what is in flight after it sends PAUSE —
≈ 2 × cable delay × line rate + sender reaction + MTU. 100 m at 400G ≈ 5 ns/m × 100 m × 2 × 400 Gb/s ≈ 50 KB, plus 2 MTUs and
NIC response ≈ 70–100 KB per lossless PG. Longer cable or faster port → larger xoff; that is what the profile name encodes.
Verify: show pfc counters (only PFC3 moves) · show queue counters (UC3 drops 0) · show pfcwd stats (storms 0) · show buffer configuration.
